title: Oath and Hollow
premise: Mirabel Kavanagh has spent her whole life guarding a sealed gate in a valley where magic cannot enter, believing the hollow inside it is empty. When the crown's witch-hunters burn the valley and drag her out, she discovers the gate was never keeping the world safe from magic — it was keeping something hungry from reaching the world, and her blood is the only lock. Fleeing across a kingdom that has erased its own magical history, she gathers a found family of hunted gift-bearers who teach her that power shared is power survived. In the end, Mirabel must reopen the gate and take the hollow into herself, becoming the living door — saving the country by vanishing from it, remembered only by the family she leaves behind.
about_author: Lior Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who grew up between two languages and one border, and writes about doors, exile, and the families we build when nations fail us. Oath and Hollow is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She performs her daily rituals at the sealed gate, feeding it salt and silence, while the valley below lives in deliberate ignorance of what she keeps. A stranger's hawk circles where no bird should fly. Emotional beat: lonely duty tinged with quiet pride, unsettled by the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Crown hunters arrive under a royal decree: all gift-bearers to be taken or burned. The village elder betrays her location to save the others; the valley burns behind her as she flees through the one door she swore never to open. Emotional beat: betrayal, grief, and the shattering of her identity as protector.

chapters.title: What Follows Her Out
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, opening on the road. She realizes something crossed the threshold with her — a cold patch of air that answers her fear. She meets Tam, a pickpocket boy whose small gift lets him hear locks, and they form an uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: terror tempered by the first spark of companionship.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Dead Places
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. He leads Mirabel to Odile, an exiled mapmaker who charts places the crown has unmade — including Vessany, the country that 'no longer exists,' which holds the only other gate. Odile agrees to guide them for a price. Emotional beat: wary hope; the map gives their flight a destination.

chapters.title: The Hunt Decree
chapters.summary: Captain Serevan's POV, the hunter leading the purge. We see his conviction that gifts are plague, and his private doubt when he burns a child's harmless charm-work. He is ordered to bring Mirabel alive — someone at court knows what she is. Emotional beat: chilling antagonist depth; ideology beginning to fray.

chapters.title: Roadside Kin
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At a smugglers' waystation the group grows: Brannoc, a disgraced hedge-knight with stone-sense, and Wren, a healer whose gift kills a little of her each time she uses it. They share a meal like a family none of them ever had. Emotional beat: warmth blooming in danger; found family takes root.

chapters.title: The Hollow Speaks
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, night watch. The thing from the gate finally shows itself — wearing her mother's voice, offering rest if she turns back. She learns the gate was sealed by her own bloodline, generation after generation, each keeper dying at their post. Emotional beat: dread and inheritance; the personal cost of the oath revealed.

chapters.title: City of Erased Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The company passes through the capital, where gifted citizens wear suppression collars and murals of old magics are scraped blank. Wren secretly heals a collared child, nearly exposing them all. Emotional beat: righteous anger; the scale of the crown's corruption made visible.

chapters.title: A Bargain with the Court
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. In the palace we meet Lord Chancellor Ivell, who wants Mirabel because her blood can open any gate — including ones into Vessany, where the crown's exiled true heir hides. Serevan accepts the mission but pockets a stolen page of Odile's maps. Emotional beat: ambition and unease; the hunt becomes political.

chapters.title: River of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Smugglers ferry them downriver; Brannoc confesses he once served the decree and helped collar a friend. The group's trust fractures and mends over an honest night of grief. Emotional beat: confession and forgiveness; the family chooses each other despite scars.

chapters.title: The Border That Isn't
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They reach where Vessany should be and find only farmland — the country literally unwritten. But Mirabel's blood hums at a fence post; the land remembers beneath the erasure. Odile begins re-inking her forbidden maps. Emotional beat: awe and defiance; hope that erased things can be restored.

chapters.title: Collars and Crows
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. His company ambushes the waystation network, torturing names out of smugglers. He captures Tam briefly; the boy escapes but leaves behind his hearing-charm, which Serevan now carries like a conscience. Emotional beat: escalating menace; the hunter haunted by what he hunts.

chapters.title: Wren's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ambushed on the moor, Wren spends too much of herself healing Brannoc and begins to fade — her hair whitening, her heartbeat thinning. Mirabel, desperate, instinctively draws on the hollow's cold power for the first time and hates how easy it feels. Emotional beat: sacrifice and temptation; power's first corrupting whisper.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Invitation
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Captured by Ivell's agents, Mirabel is offered a bargain: open the gates to Vessany willingly and her friends live. In the chancellor's vault she sees trophies of every keeper before her — including her mother's journal, revealing the hollow isn't a monster but a wound the keepers chose to carry. Emotional beat: horror and revelation; the oath reframed as love, not imprisonment.

chapters.title: Breaking the Cage
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Using his lock-hearing through Serevan's stolen charm-link, Tam guides a rescue: Brannoc unmakes the prison stones, Wren spends dangerously again, and even Serevan hesitates — then looks away at the crucial moment. They flee with the mother's journal. Emotional beat: triumph earned together; the antagonist's first mercy.

chapters.title: Ink and Old Borders
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the journal, Odile re-draws Vessany's true borders, and where her ink falls, the land remembers — roads appear, ruins stand, a dead country surfaces like a drowned body rising. The cost: every line she draws takes a memory from her. Emotional beat: bittersweet wonder; restoration always costs the restorer.

chapters.title: The Gate in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They find the second gate in a blooming orchard that shouldn't exist, guarded not by soldiers but by the ghosts of past keepers, who test Mirabel with visions of every life she'd spend. She refuses to pay with her friends and the ghosts yield, recognizing her mother's stubbornness. Emotional beat: trial and resolve; she claims the oath as her own choice.

chapters.title: Ivell's War
chapters.summary: Serevan's POV. Ivell arrives with an army, intending to force Mirabel to open the gate and seize Vessany's hidden heir and treasury. Serevan sees the collared conscripts in the ranks and finally breaks, sending warning to Mirabel via Tam's charm. Emotional beat: defection; the hunter becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: Battle of the Remembered Land
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The company, Vessan survivors drawn by Odile's maps, and Serevan's defected soldiers hold the orchard against Ivell's army. Brannoc falls shielding Tam; Wren burns the last of herself to turn the tide. Emotional beat: devastating climax of sacrifice; the family pays in blood.

chapters.title: The Door Must Be Someone
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The gate is broken by cannon-fire and the hollow pours toward the world. Mirabel understands at last: the gate was never a door in the land but in a person. She steps into the breach and takes the hollow into herself, becoming the living threshold between the countries. Emotional beat: terrible clarity and acceptance; the price of survival paid willingly.

chapters.title: Kingdom of One
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Inside the hollow, Mirabel is neither dead nor gone — she is everywhere the border runs, and through the orchard gate she speaks once more to her family, asking them to live loudly enough for both of them. Ivell is taken by his own conscripts; Serevan kneels to the restored Vessan heir. Emotional beat: transcendent sorrow; victory inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: What We Carry Through
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue. A year later, Vessany exists again on every map, and travelers cross freely through a gentle orchard gate where a warm presence watches over them. Tam, Brannoc's scarred shield on his back, plants a tree beside the gate; Wren's white-haired ghost tends it. Emotional beat: mourning braided with joy; found family endures beyond the door.
